beats.intro: Welcome to unit seven. [[q]]Statistics is the math of collecting, organizing, and making sense of data.
beats.data: Data is a collection of facts: numbers, words, or descriptions. There are two kinds. [[quant]]Quantitative data comes as numbers, things you can count or measure: [[q1]]how many students are in a class, [[q2]]or how tall each student is. [[qual]]Qualitative data describes something with words or categories: [[l1]]a favorite color, [[l2]]or the kind of pet a family owns. [[tip]]A quick test: if you can sensibly add or average the answers, it's quantitative.
beats.q1: Quick check. What kind of data?
beats.statq: A statistical question is one you expect to get many different answers to. [[one]]How old am I? There's only one answer, so it's not a statistical question. [[many]]How old are the people in my family? The answers differ, so it is a statistical question. [[var]]Answers that differ have variability: how spread out the data is. [[hi]]Ages in a family might spread from two to seventy: high variability. [[lo]]Ages in a seventh grade class cluster around twelve and thirteen: low variability.
beats.q2: Quick check. Which question is statistical?
beats.sample: Often you can't ask everyone. [[pop]]The whole group you want to know about is the population. Here, a school of two hundred students. [[samp]]A sample is a smaller part of the population that you actually ask. [[rand]]In a random sample, every member has the same chance of being chosen, so the sample tends to look like the whole population. [[bad]]If you only ask students standing in one corner, say the members of one club, the sample may not represent the whole school.
beats.estimate: A good sample lets you estimate. [[prob]]One thousand people bought snacks at a theater. You ask twenty of them, and five bought vegan snacks. [[frac]]That's five out of twenty, or one fourth, of the sample. [[scale]]Assume the same fraction holds for the whole population: one fourth of one thousand is two hundred fifty. [[ans]]About two hundred fifty people bought vegan snacks.
beats.q3: Quick check. Estimate from a sample.
beats.wrap: Statistics starts with data. [[w1]]Quantitative data is numbers; qualitative data is descriptions. [[w2]]A statistical question expects answers that vary. [[w3]]A random sample represents the population, so the fraction in the sample estimates the fraction in the whole group. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, is each question a statistical question?
beats.final3: Last one. Estimate from each sample.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter thirty-nine, introduction to statistics.
